sources.entry: WeTTY - Terminal in browser over http/https. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: WeTTY is a web-based terminal that gives browser access to a shell or SSH session over HTTP/HTTPS, using xterm.js and WebSockets.
use_cases: Accessing a server shell from a web browser
Browser-based SSH to a remote host
Giving users a terminal in a web page or iframe
Running a shell behind an nginx or traefik reverse proxy
Quick remote administration without a native SSH client
notable: Uses xterm.js for full terminal emulation in the browser
Uses WebSockets rather than Ajax for responsiveness
Runs /bin/login when started as root, otherwise ssh to localhost by default
Supports SSH password or public key auth, custom ssh config, and known hosts
Optional iframe embedding and URL-driven host/command parameters behind explicit flags
caveats: Requires an explicit trusted browser origin via --allowed-origin (or ALLOWEDORIGINS) to run
README recommends running behind a reverse proxy for HTTPS rather than exposing directly
Node.js version must be one of the patched lines listed; older Node lines are EOL
Prerequisites include make, python and build-essential
